  "name": "Magnolia Bakery's Famous Banana Pudding",
  "description": "Banana pudding has been around since the late 1800s, when faster steam ships meant bananas could make their way to US ports. It was first made with sponge cake, but by the 1920s, cake was replaced with vanilla wafers. For this recipe, Nabisco Nilla wafers are used and strongly recommended to ensure you get the same crave-worthy texture of this iconic dessert.",
  "image": [
    "https://i.shgcdn.com/d650f47e-6ae8-4ea5-a212-38991eb03e43/-/format/auto/-/quality/normal/"
  ],
  "author": {
    "@type": "Person",
    "name": "Bobbie Lloyd",
    "image": null
  },
  "datePublished": "2026-08-01T19:55:25.449217+00:00",
  "dateModified": "2026-08-01T19:55:25.449238+00:00",
  "recipeYield": "Makes 4 to 5 quarts; serves up to 16",
  "prepTime": "",
  "cookTime": "",
  "totalTime": "",
  "recipeCategory": "Dessert",
  "recipeCuisine": "American",
  "keywords": [
    "banana pudding",
    "icebox dessert",
    "vanilla wafers",
    "sweet bakes"
  ],
  "aggregateRating": {
    "@type": "AggregateRating",
    "ratingValue": 0.0,
    "reviewCount": 0
  },
  "nutrition": {
    "calories": "",
    "fatContent": "",
    "carbohydrateContent": "",
    "proteinContent": ""
  },
  "recipeIngredient": [
    "1 (3.4 ounces) package instant vanilla pudding mix, preferably Jell-O",
    "1 (14-ounce) can sweetened condensed milk",
    "1\u00bc cups (300 grams/10.6 ounces) ice-cold water",
    "3 cups (720 grams/24 ounces) heavy cream",
    "1 (11 ounces) box Nilla wafers",
    "4 large or 6 small bananas"
  ],
  "recipeInstructions": [
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 1,
      "name": "Prepare pudding mixture",
      "text": "Place the pudding mix into a 4-quart bowl and set aside. In a 2-quart liquid measuring cup or bowl with a spout, whisk together the sweetened condensed milk and water until smooth. Slowly pour the liquid into the bowl with the pudding mix while whisking constantly until thoroughly combined. Scrape the bottom and sides of the bowl with a spatula and stir until smooth.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 2,
      "name": "Chill pudding",
      "text": "Cover with plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator for a minimum of 30 minutes. The pudding can be made ahead up to 24 hours.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 3,
      "name": "Whip heavy cream",
      "text": "In a stand mixer fitted with the whisk, whip the heavy cream on medium speed for 1 minute, until the cream starts to thicken, then increase the speed to medium-high and whip until stiff peaks form. Be careful not to overwhip.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 4,
      "name": "Combine pudding and whipped cream",
      "text": "With the mixer running on low speed, add the pudding mixture a spoonful at a time. Mix until well blended and no streaks of pudding remain. Scrape the bottom and sides of the bowl.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 5,
      "name": "Assemble dessert",
      "text": "Select either a trifle bowl, a 9x13-inch pan, or a wide glass bowl with a 4- to 5-quart capacity, or individual bowls. If using a trifle bowl, spread one-quarter of the pudding over the bottom of the bowl, then layer with one-third of the cookies and enough banana slices to cover the cookie layer. Repeat the layering twice more. End with a final layer of pudding. Garnish the top with additional vanilla wafer cookies or cookie crumbs.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 6,
      "name": "Chill assembled dessert",
      "text": "Cover tightly with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 4 to 6 hours. The cookies should be tender when poked with a knife. This dessert is best served within 12 hours of assembling.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    }
  ],
  "notes": "From The Magnolia Bakery Handbook of Icebox Desserts: Classic and Creative Icebox Desserts with a Magnolia Bakery Twist, Share with Friends and Family by Bobbie Lloyd. Excerpted by permission of Harvest, an imprint of HarperCollins.",

  "name": "Overnight Mac & Cheese",
  "description": "This is the easiest, cheesiest, crustiest mac & cheese I've ever made! It's the perfect prep-ahead dish; you don't even need to make a roux. Prepare the mixture a day ahead, refrigerate it overnight, pour it into an ovenproof dish, and bake it before dinner.",
  "image": [

  ],

  },

  ],
  "aggregateRating": {
    "@type": "AggregateRating",
    "ratingValue": 0.0,
    "reviewCount": 0
  },
  "nutrition": {
    "calories": "",
    "fatContent": "",
    "carbohydrateContent": "",
    "proteinContent": ""
  },
  "recipeIngredient": [
    "Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper",
    "12 ounces cavatappi pasta",
    "4\u00bd cups heavy cream",
    "3 cups grated Gruy\u00e8re cheese, divided (8 ounces)",
    "1\u00bd cups grated sharp white Cheddar, such as Cabot, divided (4 ounces)",
    "\u00bd teaspoon ground nutmeg",
    "3 tablespoons melted unsalted butter, plus extra for the dish",
    "2\u00bd cups fresh white breadcrumbs",
    "6 slices white bread (for breadcrumbs)"
  ],
  "recipeInstructions": [
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 1,
      "name": "Make the breadcrumbs",
      "text": "For 2\u00bd cups of breadcrumbs, remove the crusts from 6 slices of white bread and dice. Place in the bowl of a food processor fitted with the steel blade and process until finely ground.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 2,
      "name": "Cook the pasta",
      "text": "A day before you plan to serve, bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add 2 tablespoons salt and the pasta and cook for 4 minutes (it will be undercooked). Drain (don't rinse) and set aside.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 3,
      "name": "Combine cream and cheese",
      "text": "In a medium (10-inch) bowl, combine the cream, 1\u00bd cups of the Gruy\u00e8re, \u00be cup of the cheddar, the nutmeg, 1 tablespoon salt, and 1\u00bd teaspoons pepper.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 4,
      "name": "Mix and refrigerate",
      "text": "Stir the hot pasta into the cream mixture, cover the bowl with plastic, and refrigerate for 24 hours. The pasta will absorb the cream and expand.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 5,
      "name": "Bring to room temperature",
      "text": "When ready to bake, allow the mixture to sit at room temperature for about one hour. (You can also microwave it for 4 minutes.)",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 6,
      "name": "Prepare for baking",
      "text": "Preheat the oven to 400 degrees. Butter a 9x13 2-inch baking dish. Stir the pasta mixture well, transfer it to the dish, and spread it evenly.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 7,
      "name": "Add cheese topping",
      "text": "Combine the remaining 1\u00bd cups Gruy\u00e8re and \u00be cup Cheddar and sprinkle evenly on top.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 8,
      "name": "Add breadcrumb topping",
      "text": "Combine the breadcrumbs and the 3 tablespoons melted butter and sprinkle evenly over the cheese.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 9,
      "name": "Bake",
      "text": "Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, rotating halfway through, until golden brown. Serve hot.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    }
  ],

    "story": "Gratins are a defining technique of French home cooking, traceable to the 18th-century kitchens of the Dauphin\u00e9 region where cooks layered sliced vegetables with cream and breadcrumbs to make humble produce keep longer and taste richer. The word itself comes from the French verb gratter \u2014 to scrape \u2014 referring to the browned crust that forms on top. Asparagus arrived in this tradition somewhat later, prized as a seasonal luxury in the Loire Valley and around Paris, where white asparagus in particular became a springtime ritual.\n\nThe combination of the vegetable's sweetness with a creamy b\u00e9chamel and a crisp gruy\u00e8re topping is now classical in France, but this particular version \u2014 with its Italian herbs (oregano, basil, parsley) and blend of parmesan and mozzarella \u2014 reflects the broader European and North American adoption of the gratin form. The Italian and Italian-American kitchen embraced the technique enthusiastically, adapting it to local cheese traditions and the Mediterranean herb palette.\n\nTraditionally the dish is served as a starter or vegetable course at Sunday lunch in spring, often alongside roast lamb, veal, or chicken.   "editorial": {
    "opinion": "This is a straightforward vegetable gratin that leans on cheese and herbs rather than a b\u00e9chamel or cream base\u2014a lighter approach than classical French gratins. The cook is asked to blanch or roast asparagus, toss it with melted butter and aromatics, then top with a modest cheese blend (parmesan for sharpness, mozzarella for melt) and broil until golden. The herb ratio (oregano, parsley, basil at 1/2 teaspoon each) is restrained, which works if the asparagus is fresh and the parmesan is aged; it wobbles if either ingredient is bland or if the mozzarella drowns out the vegetable's delicate flavor.\n\nThis suits home cooks after a quick, unfussy side\u2014no roux, no stock, no long oven time.       "name": "Prepare the crust",
      "text": "Preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Place an 8-inch deep-dish pie plate or 9-inch pie plate on a baking sheet. Place the margarine in a medium microwave-safe bowl and heat on HIGH for 45 seconds or until melted. Stir in the walnuts and brown sugar; mix until combined. Transfer to the pie plate and press to cover the bottom and about 1 inch up the sides. Bake for 15 minutes so the crust is firm and set. Transfer to a wire rack to cool; leave the oven on.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 2,
      "name": "Make the filling",
      "text": "Combine the eggs, yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl; set the bowl over a medium saucepan filled with a few inches of barely bubbling water, over medium heat. Stir to combine the egg mixture, then zest 6 of the Key limes (about a tablespoon) over the mixture. Squeeze the juice from those 6 plus the remaining 8 Key limes and stir it into the mixture (1/2 cup total). Cook uncovered for about 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, to form a thick custard. Be patient and do not stir too much. Remove from the heat. Whisk in the margarine in small pieces until the cream is smooth. Stir in the green food coloring, if using.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 3,
      "name": "Bake the pie",
      "text": "Pour the filling into the prepared crust, spreading it evenly. Bake (with the pie plate on the baking sheet) for 20 minutes (at 350 degrees) or until the outside edges of the filling are set; the inside can remain a little jiggly. Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 4,
      "name": "Prepare the meringue topping",
      "text": "Combine the water and sugar in a small saucepan over high heat, stirring to dissolve the sugar. Cook without stirring until the mixture reaches 230 degrees; dip a pastry brush in water and use it to brush down any sugar crystals that might form on the sides of the saucepan. Meanwhile, beat the egg whites in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a balloon whisk attachment or a hand-held electric mixer on low speed to start, then on high speed to form stiff peaks. Reduce the speed to low; gradually add the cooked sugar mixture, letting it fall along the side of the bowl and not directly onto the egg whites or the whisk attachment. When all of the cooked sugar mixture has been added, increase the speed to medium-high; beat for 1 or 2 minutes to form a thick, shiny meringue.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {

      "name": "Finish the pie",
      "text": "Use a silicone spatula to spread the meringue evenly over the pie filling. If desired, use a culinary torch to lightly brown the surface of the meringue.     {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 1,
      "name": "Prepare pan",
      "text": "Grease a Bundt pan and spread pecans on the bottom of the pan.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 2,
      "name": "Mix wet ingredients",
      "text": "Beat eggs, oil, water, and rum in a mixer just until incorporated.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 3,
      "name": "Add dry ingredients",
      "text": "Add pudding mix and cake mix and beat on medium for about 3 to 5 minutes just until you get a smooth texture.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 4,
      "name": "Bake cake",
      "text": "Pour into pan and bake at 350 degrees for 40 to 45 minutes. The cake should have a light golden-brown color but will darken with the glaze.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 5,
      "name": "Make glaze",
      "text": "Melt butter in a saucepan and add the sugar and water, bring to a boil. Once it starts to boil, take off the heat and add the rum. Pour into a large measuring cup that will hold that amount or more. Set aside.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 6,
      "name": "Apply glaze to cake",
      "text": "Once the cake is ready, take it out of the oven and leave it in the pan. Gently prick holes into the cake with a skewer. Slowly pour half of the glaze over the cake making sure to fill in all the holes. Once the cake has soaked up the glaze, turn the cake over, removing the pan, onto the base that the cake will stay on. Gently prick more holes on the other side and slowly pour the other half of the glaze over the cake.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 7,
      "name": "Finish and cool",
      "text": "Fill the center of the cake with reserved pecans. Let cool and enjoy. The cake is best if left at room temperature.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    }
  ],
  "notes": "The glaze needs to be prepared approximately 10 minutes before the cake is ready. Make sure you have plenty of paper towels underneath the base as the glaze will run down the sides of the cake.",

  "name": "Citrus Marmalade",
  "description": "Tangy and loaded with candied peel, this marmalade is as delicious on toast as it is over grilled pork. The tastier the fruit, the better the marmalade, so use citrus you like eating fresh. Stick with one or mix and match whatever you find.",
  "image": [
    "https://www.gannett-cdn.com/-mm-/eb25b9fc80fedfbd092d42771dd48d5f08ccfeb5/c=0-364-3889-2552/local/-/media/2020/09/17/Hyannis/ghows-CC-200609811-eedd4e5e.jpg?width=660&height=372&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp"

    "1 large lemon",
    "5 cups granulated sugar"
  ],
  "recipeInstructions": [
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 1,
      "name": "Prepare the citrus",
      "text": "Place the sweet citrus and lemon in a colander. If they have wax on them, turn your kitchen tap to the hottest setting and run the hot water over them while shaking the colander. Whether waxed or unwaxed, run cool water over the citrus while scrubbing them with a vegetable brush. Drain well, then trim and discard the stem ends of the sweet citrus; reserve the lemon. Cut the sweet citrus, including the pith and peel, into a 1/4-inch dice, discarding any seeds. Transfer the cut fruit and any accumulated juices to a large saucepan.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 2,
      "name": "Simmer the fruit",
      "text": "Using a Microplane grater, zest the lemon directly over the cut fruit. Squeeze the juice from the lemon and add to the saucepan. Add enough water to cover the fruit, about 6 cups, then bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to medium-low to maintain a steady simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until the fruit peel is very soft, 40 to 45 minutes.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 3,
      "name": "Sterilize the jars",
      "text": "Meanwhile, bring a large, wide pot of water to a boil. Using tongs, carefully lower 6 (half-pint) canning jars into the boiling water. Immerse the ladle or spoon you're going to use for filling the jars too. Boil for 10 minutes, then drop in the jars' lids and remove from the heat. Keep everything in the hot water until ready to use.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 4,
      "name": "Cook with sugar to setting point",
      "text": "Raise the heat under the fruit to bring the mixture back to a rapid boil. Clip in a candy thermometer if you have one. If not, put a large metal spoon in the freezer. Add the sugar and stir carefully to evenly incorporate it. Continue boiling and stirring often until the mixture reaches 220 degrees F for a runnier marmalade or 223 degrees F for a stiffer one, 25 to 30 minutes. To test its doneness without a thermometer, drop a dollop onto the spoon from the freezer. Let it sit for 15 seconds, then tilt the spoon. That will be the consistency of the finished product. A stiff marmalade won't budge and a looser one will move like lava.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 5,
      "name": "Fill the jars",
      "text": "Transfer the jars from the hot water to a clean kitchen towel on the counter. Shake out any water inside, then divide the marmalade among the jars with the sterilized ladle, filling them to \u00bd inch from the top. If any spills onto the threads, dip a clean paper towel into the hot water and wipe off any stickiness. Screw on the lids until just tight.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 6,
      "name": "Process the jars",
      "text": "If you have a jar rack or other metal rack that fits in the pot, center it in the hot water. Otherwise, push a clean kitchen towel against the bottom of the pot. Bring the water back to a boil, then carefully lower in the filled jars with canning clamps or tongs, making sure they don't touch each other. The water should be at least an inch above the jars. If not, add more.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 7,
      "name": "Cool and seal",
      "text": "Boil for 10 minutes, then remove from the heat. Using the clamps or tongs, carefully transfer the jars back to the kitchen towel on the counter. Let stand for at least a day before opening. When the jars are room temperature, label with the date and the types of fruits you used. As the jars continue to cool, you should hear the lids pop. If any don't, that means they didn't seal properly and won't be shelf-stable, so transfer those jars to the refrigerator after they've cooled to room temperature and eat within four months.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Marmalades take longer to make than most jams because you need to boil the citrus skins into tenderness and boil away the bitterness of their pith. Once the sugar goes in, the mix needs to cook again to infuse the peel with sweetness and thicken the syrup into something spreadable. It takes a few hours \u2014 which is a good thing when trying to pass the time at home on a weekend. The results are as delicious spooned on toast as they are over grilled pork or chicken.",

      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 1,
      "name": "Cook the onions",
      "text": "Cook the onions slowly in butter in a small saucepan for 5 minutes or so, until tender and translucent but not browned. Stir in the shallots or onions, and garlic, and cook slowly for 1 minute more. Set aside.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 2,
      "name": "Prepare the scallops",
      "text": "Dry the scallops and cut into slices 1/4 inch thick. Just before cooking, sprinkle with salt and pepper, roll in flour, and shake off excess flour.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 3,
      "name": "Saut\u00e9 the scallops",
      "text": "Saut\u00e9 the scallops quickly in very hot butter and oil for 2 minutes to brown them lightly.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 4,
      "name": "Simmer with wine and herbs",
      "text": "Pour the wine, or the vermouth and water, into the skillet with the scallops. Add the herbs and the cooked onion mixture. Cover the skillet and simmer for 5 minutes. Then uncover, and if necessary boil down the sauce rapidly for a minute until it is lightly thickened. Correct seasoning, and discard bay leaf.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 5,
      "name": "Fill the shells",
      "text": "Spoon the scallops and sauce into the shells. Sprinkle with cheese and dot with butter. Set aside or refrigerate until ready to gratin\u00e9.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 6,
      "name": "Broil and serve",
      "text": "Just before serving, run under a moderately hot broiler for 3 to 4 minutes to heat through, and to brown the cheese lightly.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    }
  ],

      "name": "Prepare the sauce",
      "text": "Heat olive oil in a heavy pot. Add onion and saut\u00e9 until transparent. Add garlic and stir. Add tomatoes and herbs. Bring sauce to bubbling and turn down heat to simmer. Let cook, stirring occasionally, until it begins to thicken, while you prepare the rest of the ingredients. If you're making the sauce in advance, cook for about 45 minutes to an hour, then refrigerate. You'll need 2 cups for your chicken; the rest can be frozen.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 2,
      "name": "Prepare the chicken",
      "text": "If you buy the chicken as 2 skinless breasts, cut each breast in half lengthwise. Put chicken between 2 sheets of waxed paper and pound to make it evenly thick, about one-half to three-quarters of an inch. Put egg white and water in a shallow bowl. Beat lightly. Dip cutlets in egg wash. Spread some panko on waxed paper. Cover the cutlets with panko, pressing the crumbs into the chicken.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 3,
      "name": "Cook the chicken",
      "text": "Put 1 tablespoon olive oil in large frying pan and heat to medium high. Add chicken and cook about 3 minutes, until golden. Add the second tablespoon of olive oil when turning chicken. Cook 2 minutes more.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 4,
      "name": "Assemble and bake",
      "text": "To assemble the chicken Parmigiana, spread 1 cup of sauce in the bottom of a shallow baking dish that will hold the chicken in 1 layer. Spread another cup of sauce over the chicken. Bake for about 15 minutes at 350\u00b0 F. Remove dish from oven and sprinkle with shredded mozzarella. Return dish to oven for 5 minutes and turn off the heat. The cheese doesn't need to cook, just melt. Serve with whole wheat thin spaghetti and a salad.",

      "imageCredit": null
    }

    "opinion": "This is a straightforward creamed-butter cake that leans heavily on fruit and spice to carry flavor\u2014and the ratios reflect that gamble. With only 1/4 teaspoon each of cinnamon and ginger, plus 1/8 teaspoon cloves across a full cake, the spicing is genuinely restrained; you're tasting apple first, warm notes second. The formula itself is conventional (butter, sugar, eggs, flour, baking soda), but the cook is asked to do something smart: fold in 4 cups of chopped raw apples and raisins directly into batter, which means managing moisture carefully. That much fruit will release liquid as it bakes, so the cake's texture hinges on the balance between the baking soda (which helps set crumb quickly) and the fruit's own hydration. The result should be moist without collapsing\u2014ideal for someone who wants an apple cake that tastes like apples, not a spice cake that happens to contain them.   "description": "Flour's addictive sticky buns have been famous in Boston for many years, but they got national attention in the spring of 2007, when they starred in an episode of the Food Network show Throwdown with Bobby Flay. These sticky buns are quite simply the stickiest, richest, gooiest, most decadent buns you'll ever have. We start them with a brioche dough base and then fill them with sugar, pecans, and cinnamon and top them with copious amounts of a sticky caramel concoction called, naturally, goo.",

  "recipeInstructions": [
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 1,
      "name": null,
      "text": "In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook attachment, combine the all-purpose flour, bread flour, yeast, sugar, salt, water, and 5 eggs in the bowl. Mix on low speed until all the ingredients have come together, 3 to 4 minutes. Scrape the bowl if necessary to make sure all the flour is incorporated into the wet ingredients. Mix on low speed for another 3 to 4 minutes once the dough has all come together. It will be very stiff.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 2,
      "name": null,
      "text": "Add the butter to the flour mixture piece by piece, and continue mixing on low speed for about 10 minutes. The butter needs to mix completely into the dough so stop the mixer occasionally and scrape the sides of the bowl and break up the dough with your hands if necessary to help the butter mix in.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 3,
      "name": null,
      "text": "Once the butter is completely incorporated into the dough, mix on medium speed for another 15 minutes, until the dough becomes sticky and soft and somewhat shiny. Turn the mixer up to medium-high speed for about 1 minute and you should hear it make a slap-slap-slap sound as the dough hits the sides of the bowl. Test the dough by pulling at it\u2014when you pull at the dough it should stretch a bit and have a little give. If it seems wet and loose and more like a batter than a dough, add a few tablespoons of flour and mix until it comes together. If it breaks off into pieces when you pull at it, continue to mix it on medium for another 2 to 3 minutes until it develops more strength and stretches when you grab it. You should be able to gather it all together and pick it up all as one piece when it's ready.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 4,
      "name": null,
      "text": "Place the dough in a large bowl or plastic container and cover the dough with plastic wrap\u2014the plastic wrap should be directly on top of the dough, touching it. Let the dough proof (i.e., grow and develop flavor) in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours or overnight.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 5,
      "name": null,
      "text": "Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Divide the Basic Brioche dough in half; use 1 half for this recipe and reserve the other half for another use.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 6,
      "name": null,
      "text": "On a floured work surface roll the brioche into a tall rectangle, about 12x16 inches, and \u00bc inch thick. It will have the consistency of cold damp Play-Doh and it should be fairly easy to roll out.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 7,
      "name": null,
      "text": "In a small bowl, mix together the brown sugar, white sugar, ground cinnamon, and half of the chopped pecans. Sprinkle this mixture evenly over the entire surface of the brioche rectangle.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 8,
      "name": null,
      "text": "Starting from the top (12-inch edge) of the rectangle and working your way down, roll the brioche-like a jelly roll until the entire sheet is rolled up. Roll tightly so you have a nice round spiral. Trim both edges of the brioche roll about \u00bc inch to even out the ends.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 9,
      "name": null,
      "text": "Using a bench scraper or a chef's knife, cut the roll into 8 equal pieces about 1\u00bd inches wide. (At this point the unbaked buns can be tightly wrapped and frozen for up to 1 week. When ready to bake, remove the buns from freezer. Leave them wrapped and let them defrost in the refrigerator overnight, or at room temperature for 2 to 3 hours; proceed as directed.)",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 10,
      "name": null,
      "text": "Pour the Goo into a 9x13-inch baking dish and sprinkle the remaining pecans evenly over the Goo. Place the buns in the pan, evenly spaced. Cover the dish with plastic wrap and let the buns proof at warm room temperature for about 2 hours, until the dough is puffy, pillowy, and soft and the buns are touching.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 11,
      "name": null,
      "text": "Heat the oven to 350 degrees and position a rack in the middle of the oven.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 12,
      "name": null,
      "text": "Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until the buns are golden brown. Remove from the oven and let cool for 20 to 30 minutes in the dish. Invert the buns one at a time onto a serving platter and spoon any extra Goo and pecans on top. Serve warm.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 13,
      "name": null,
      "text": "(These are best served right away, or within 4 hours of baking. You could make them 1 day and serve them the next after warming them in a 325-degree oven for 10 to 12 minutes, but at Flour we don't serve the day-old version of this treat.)",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 14,
      "name": null,
      "text": "In a medium saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat and whisk in the brown sugar until the sugar is dissolved. Remove the pan from the heat and whisk in the honey, heavy cream, water, and salt. Let cool to room temperature before using, about 30 minutes. Goo can be made up to 2 weeks in advance and stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    }
  ],
  "notes": "These sticky buns are best enjoyed warm from the oven. You can also re-heat them up to 1 day later in a 300-degree oven for 5 to 7 minutes to get the full ooey gooey effect. When you eat them, be sure to have plenty of napkins nearby.",

I went head-to-head with Chef Flay in a sticky bun bakeoff\u2014in front of TV cameras and a live audience of about 100 customers at Flour. After we both finished baking our buns, for an agonizing hour customers were quizzed about which buns they preferred, mine or Chef Flay\u2019s, while the judges privately did their judging. We won! Many people wonder if the judging on television shows is fixed; the visible sweat on my brow during the judging should assure them that it is most definitely not. These sticky buns are quite simply the stickiest, richest, gooiest, most decadent buns you\u2019ll ever have. We start them with a brioche dough base and then fill them with sugar, pecans, and cinnamon and top them with copious amounts of a sticky caramel concoction called, naturally, goo. When you eat them, be sure to have plenty of napkins nearby. These are best enjoyed warm from the oven; you can also re-heat them up to 1 day later in a 300-degree oven for 5 to 7 minutes to get the full ooey gooey effect.\n\n![Joanne Chang's Sticky Sticky Buns](//cherrybombe.com/cdn/shop/articles/Sticky_Buns_1_Kristin_Teig_0d4c4058-d167-47e0-86d9-d949254e0e18.jpg?v=1711555810&width=1765)\n\n![Joanne Chang's Sticky Sticky Buns](//cherrybombe.com/cdn/shop/articles/Sticky_Buns_1_Kristin_Teig_0d4c4058-d167-47e0-86d9-d949254e0e18.jpg?v=1711555810&width=1765)\n\n##\n\n##\n\n###\n\n## Image Credits\n\nPhoto by Kristin Teig\n\n## Ingredients\n\n### For THE sticky buns\n\n* Basic Brioche dough (recipe follows)\n* \u00bc cup (60 grams) light brown sugar\n* \u00bc cup (50 grams) granulated sugar\n* \u215b teaspoon ground cinnamon\n* 1 cup (100 grams) pecan halves, toasted and chopped\n* 1 recipe Goo (recipe follows)\n\n### FOR THE BASIC BRIOCHE DOUGH\n\n* Makes 2 loaves\n* 2\u00bd cups (350 grams) all-purpose flour\n* 2\u00bd cups (375 grams) high-gluten bread flour\n* 1\u00bd packages (3\u00bc teaspoons) active dry yeast or 28 grams fresh cake yeast\n* \u2153 cup plus 2 tablespoons (92 grams) sugar\n* 1 tablespoon salt\n* \u2154 cup cold water\n* 5 large eggs, plus 1 egg for egg wash\n* 22 tablespoons (2\u00be sticks; 310 grams) unsalted butter at room temperature, cut into 10 to 12 pieces\n\n### for the goo\n\n* Makes about 2 cups (enough for 8 buns)\n* \u00be cup (1\u00bd sticks; 168 grams) unsalted butter\n* 1\u00bd cups (345 grams) light brown sugar\n* \u2153 cup (110 grams) honey\n* \u2153 cup (80 grams) heavy cream\n* \u2153 cup (75 grams) water\n* \u00bc teaspoon salt\n\n## Method\n\n1. **Make the Basic Brioche:** In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook attachment, combine the all-purpose flour, bread flour, yeast, sugar, salt, water, and 5 eggs in the bowl. Mix on low speed until all the ingredients have come together, 3 to 4 minutes. Scrape the bowl if necessary to make sure all the flour is incorporated into the wet ingredients. Mix on low speed for another 3 to 4 minutes once the dough has all come together. It will be very stiff.\n2. Add the butter to the flour mixture piece by piece, and continue mixing on low speed for about 10 minutes. The butter needs to mix completely into the dough so stop the mixer occasionally and scrape the sides of the bowl and break up the dough with your hands if necessary to help the butter mix in.\n3. Once the butter is completely incorporated into the dough, mix on medium speed for another 15 minutes, until the dough becomes sticky and soft and somewhat shiny. Turn the mixer up to medium-high speed for about 1 minute and you should hear it make a slap-slap-slap sound as the dough hits the sides of the bowl. Test the dough by pulling at it\u2014when you pull at the dough it should stretch a bit and have a little give. If it seems wet and loose and more like a batter than a dough, add a few tablespoons of flour and mix until it comes together. If it breaks off into pieces when you pull at it, continue to mix it on medium for another 2 to 3 minutes until it develops more strength and stretches when you grab it. You should be able to gather it all together and pick it up all as one piece when it\u2019s ready.\n4. Place the dough in a large bowl or plastic container and cover the dough with plastic wrap\u2014the plastic wrap should be directly on top of the dough, touching it. Let the dough proof (i.e., grow and develop flavor) in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours or overnight.\n5. **Make the sticky buns:** Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Divide the Basic Brioche dough in half; use 1 half for this recipe and reserve the other half for another use.\n6. On a floured work surface roll the brioche into a tall rectangle, about 12x16 inches, and \u00bc inch thick. It will have the consistency of cold damp Play-Doh and it should be fairly easy to roll out.\n7. In a small bowl, mix together the brown sugar, white sugar, ground cinnamon, and half of the chopped pecans. Sprinkle this mixture evenly over the entire surface of the brioche rectangle.\n8. Starting from the top (12-inch edge) of the rectangle and working your way down, roll the brioche-like a jelly roll until the entire sheet is rolled up. Roll tightly so you have a nice round spiral. Trim both edges of the brioche roll about \u00bc inch to even out the ends.\n9. Using a bench scraper or a chef\u2019s knife, cut the roll into 8 equal pieces about 1\u00bd inches wide. (At this point the unbaked buns can be tightly wrapped and frozen for up to 1 week. When ready to bake, remove the buns from freezer. Leave them wrapped and let them defrost in the refrigerator overnight, or at room temperature for 2 to 3 hours; proceed as directed.)\n10. Pour the Goo into a 9x13-inch baking dish and sprinkle the remaining pecans evenly over the Goo. Place the buns in the pan, evenly spaced. Cover the dish with plastic wrap and let the buns proof at warm room temperature for about 2 hours, until the dough is puffy, pillowy, and soft and the buns are touching.\n11. Heat the oven to 350 degrees and position a rack in the middle of the oven.\n12. Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until the buns are golden brown. Remove from the oven and let cool for 20 to 30 minutes in the dish. Invert the buns one at a time onto a serving platter and spoon any extra Goo and pecans on top. Serve warm.\n13. (These are best served right away, or within 4 hours of baking. You could make them 1 day and serve them the next after warming them in a 325-degree oven for 10 to 12 minutes, but at Flour we don\u2019t serve the day-old version of this treat.)\n14. **Make the goo:** In a medium saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat and whisk in the brown sugar until the sugar is dissolved. Remove the pan from the heat and whisk in the honey, heavy cream, water, and salt. Let cool to room temperature before using, about 30 minutes.
